name: Hereditary Leiomyomatosis and Renal Cell Cancer

criteria.description: Presence of multiple cutaneous piloleiomyomas confirmed by histopathology
Early-onset multiple uterine leiomyomas in females
Diagnosis of type 2 papillary renal cell carcinoma or other RCC subtypes associated with HLRCC
Identification of pathogenic germline FH gene mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic FH gene mutation plus either multiple cutaneous leiomyomas or early-onset uterine leiomyomas or renal cell carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation; histopathology supports diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Firm, painful skin nodules typically on trunk and limbs
Large, symptomatic fibroids often requiring early intervention
Aggressive renal cancer subtype associated with HLRCC

common.notes: Pain exacerbated by cold or pressure
Heavy menstrual bleeding common in affected females

common.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass from uterine fibroids
common.notes: Large fibroids may be clinically detectable
Gross or microscopic blood in urine

occasional.notes: Non-specific symptom related to chronic disease burden
May be related to renal tumors or cysts

occasional.symptomName: Skin hyperpigmentation or discoloration over leiomyomas

occasional.notes: Due to uterine leiomyomas affecting uterine function

rare.notes: Symptoms related to distant spread such as bone pain or neurological deficits
Rare malignant transformation of cutaneous leiomyomas
Rare hematologic or metabolic abnormalities related to RCC

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in advanced RCC
imaging: MRI or CT showing multiple uterine leiomyomas
CT or MRI detecting renal masses, often aggressive papillary RCC
Skin ultrasound or MRI for cutaneous nodules
genetic: Pathogenic germline mutations in the fumarate hydratase (FH) gene
other: Histopathological confirmation of piloleiomyomas and RCC subtype
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: No increased risk of renal cell carcinoma
Different renal tumor types (clear cell RCC)
VHL gene mutation instead of FH

redFlags: Family history of renal cell carcinoma or leiomyomas
references: Launonen V, et al. Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC). J Med Genet. 2001.
Tomlinson IPM, et al. Germline mutations in FH predispose to dominantly inherited uterine fibroids, skin leiomyomata and papillary renal cell cancer. Nat Genet. 2002.
Menko FH, et al. Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC): renal cancer risk, surveillance and treatment. Fam Cancer. 2014.
